newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala not to cool Taiwan ties despite veto.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala not to cool Taiwan ties despite veto.

text.p: Guatemala will not cool relations with Taiwan even if that would persuade China to overturn its veto on sending the country a U.N. peacekeeping mission, a government official said on Thursday.

"We have been friends with Taiwan since the island has existed as an independent country. Guatemala's position on Taiwan will be maintained. It will not vary," presidential spokesman Ricardo de la Torre told a news conference.

China vetoed a resolution before the U.N. security council last week to send 155 military observers to Guatemala to monitor U.N.-brokered peace agreements that ended more than three decades of civil war. The 14 other council members supported the resolution.
Chinese officials hinted on Thursday that Guatemala should sever ties with Taiwan, which China considers a renegade province, if it wanted Beijing to reconsider the veto.

Shen Guofang, spokesman for China's Foreign Relations Ministry in Beijing, said Guatemala was violating U.N. principles by maintaining diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which does not have U.N. representation.
De la Torre ruled out an apology to China for Guatemala's support of U.N. membership for Taipei and its invitation to Taiwan to attend a ceremony celebrating Guatemala's peace treaty last December.
"We don't have to apologise to anybody. In this case no way. We are independent and free to decide who are our allies and who are our friends," De la Torre said.

Guatemala has said it would go to the Organisation of American States to seek an alternative group of monitors, but it continues to angle for the U.N. observers, seeing them as lending international credibility to the disarming of Guatemalan rebels.
Guatemalan and Chinese diplomats in the United States held talks on Wednesday and Thursday in an effort to repair the rift. De la Torre said he could not comment on the talks.
Taiwan is among the five biggest foreign investors in Guatemala, where it has built textile-assembly factories, retail businesses, and power plants.
